title: Tavuk Sote
subtitle: Turkish chicken saute with pepper and tomato
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs cooked in a quick pan sauce of tomatoes, green and red peppers, and a touch of paprika. This is a fast Turkish weeknight dish that needs nothing but rice or flatbread alongside.
sourceNotes: A common Turkish home dish found across the country. Sote simply means saute, and this version follows the standard tomato-pepper base used in everyday Turkish cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions with the sauce. Defrost in the fridge overnight and reheat in a covered pan over low heat.
recipe.batchNotes: Use two pans to keep the chicken from steaming. Combine both into one pan once the peppers are added.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cooks fast enough to make fresh each time, but the sauce holds well in the fridge for 2 days.

content.text: Tavuk sote is a Turkish pan-cooked chicken dish with a tomato and pepper sauce. Brown the chicken properly before the vegetables go in; the colour builds the flavour. The sauce should be fairly thick by the time the dish is done.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer. Do not stir for 3 minutes. Turn and colour the other side. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining oil. Fry the onion for 5 minutes until it softens.
Add both peppers and the garlic. Cook for 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peppers soften at the edges.
Stir in the tomato puree and both paprikas. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and 100 ml of water. Stir and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken to the pan. Stir to coat. Cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and black pepper. Scatter the parsley over and serve with rice or bread.

items.symptom: The chicken releases a lot of liquid and stews instead of colours.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough, or too much chicken went in at once.
items.fix: Cook in smaller batches over a high heat. A crowded pan drops the temperature and prevents browning.
Cook uncovered for an extra 5 to 10 minutes on medium heat until the sauce reduces to a coating consistency.

items.cause: They were cooked too long before the chicken went back in.
items.fix: Add the peppers after the onion has softened and move quickly; they only need a few minutes to lose their raw edge.
